messages:
erin: cs escalation — several customers reporting 503s on /v1/embeddings since ~09:12 UTC. CS pasted one stacktrace, looks like upstream runner coredump during large-batch prefetch. customers impacted: acme, helios, internal-dev. filing here for triage.

sam: oncall ack. spinning up traces now. can you drop the sample stack and one request log? also did CS note any common request shape (batch size / model)?

erin: pasted logs below (sanitized):
```
[09:11:58.241] runner: segfault (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f8b2c1f
#0  0x7f8b2c1f in kv_prefetch::copy()
#1  0x7f9a3b2a in runtime::dispatch_batch()
#2  0x55aa12ff in start_thread
```
request headers: X-Client: acme, model: phi-embed-1.0-q4, batch_size: 64, concurrency: 8

incidentbot: Alert: hosted-infer.runner_crash_count spike — 14 crashes in 12m. p95 embed latency 3200ms -> 12s.

maria: adding eng-runtime. earliest hypothesis: mem-fragmentation or KV prefetch race under large batch+quant combo. cc @lee for native logs.

lee: quick note — i reproduced a local crash on dev-gpu1 with the same model and batch=64 + concurrency=6. backtrace shows pagefault in NV kernel during prefetch. attaching gdb snippet: 
```
#0  0x00007f9b1a2b13e7 in cuMemcpyAsync
#1  0x00007f9b2245a1b2 in kv_prefetch_gpu
#2  0x000055aa12ff in dispatch
```

lee: repro steps i used: 
1) start runner with `RUNNER_PREFETCH=1` and `KV_CACHE=on`
2) send embed requests: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"phi-embed-1.0-q4","inputs":[...64 items...]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'`
3) concurrency via `wrk` approx 6 threads, payload size 64

erin: customers reported this after we rolled quant swap for phi-embed yesterday at 02:00 UTC. could be related.

sam: mitigation applied: temporarily set routing rule to avoid quantized variant for embeddings (route phi-embed-1.0-q4 -> phi-embed-1.0-fp16) for hosted-pool-3. also lowered max_batch_size to 32 via feature-flag. monitoring now.

jim: confirmed routing change applied, flagged impacted customers and sent canned CS note. will hold until 09:40 to see crash count drop.

maria: action items for eng-runtime: 1) collect full coredump + nvml logs from nodes that crashed and upload to incidents bucket, 2) reproduce with `NV_PREFETCH_DEBUG=1`, 3) add guard to reject batch_size>48 for quantized models until root cause found.

lee: uploading artifacts: s3://redwood-incident/9350002468/{gdb.txt, nvml.log, runner.metrics}. I've also preserved one core under /var/crash/core.

sam: plan: triage on-call repro today, try running with workaround (disable prefetch) and test perf. if stable, rollback quant swap for hosted by 18:00 UTC and schedule deeper kernel debugging. please add timeline in incident doc. @erin assign CS followups.

erin: assigned, sending CS update now. thanks all for fast response :thumbsup:

maria: earned note — possible long-term fixes: safer prefetch path (bounds checks), backpressure on KV prefetch queue, and more aggressive batching caps per model-variant. I'll open follow-up PRs + RFC.

incidentbot: Incident log appended: 9350002468. status: mitigation in place, monitoring ongoing.
